registered_before: any multi-day return of this rule, or of any momentum ranking, was computed on 2016-2026. Daily bars for these years were downloaded earlier only to pick opening candidates for the opening breakout studies (#788, #796); no study held a position overnight on them. The rule comes from a NotebookLM summary of Grimes, Bellafiore and Sinclair plus momentum papers (relative strength leaders, quiet pullback to the 20-day average, early time exit), fixed here before any data was read. Already known: opening range breakouts on stocks in play lose money after real fills (#803), and intraday price-only setups showed no edge, which is why this test uses a multi-day hold where costs are small next to the move.
question: Do US stocks that lead the market over six months, bought the morning after a quiet three-day pullback to their 20-day average and held up to ten sessions, beat the market after costs, and does the pullback timing beat simply buying the same kind of leader that day?
why_it_matters: The owner wants a repeatable setup. This one trades long stock or long calls in a Roth IRA, is checked once a day after the close, and holds long enough that spreads are small next to the expected move.
sessions: signals on regular sessions from 2016-07-01 (the first with six months of SIP history) to 2026-10-28 (so every hold ends by 2026-11-12), New York; entries and exits on the following sessions

data.names: common stocks on any of Polygon's reference snapshots already saved for the opening breakout studies: 2016-01-04, 2016-07-01 and every six months to 2024-01-02, then 2024-07-01, 2025-01-02, 2025-07-01, 2026-01-02, 2026-06-12 and 2026-11-12; symbols of capital letters with an optional .X class. Names later delisted are included
data.daily: Alpaca SIP daily bars 2016-01-04 to 2026-11-12 for every name, split-adjusted (prices and volume) and unadjusted closes (for the price filter and the cent cost); SPY and QQQ split-adjusted
data.dividends: not added to the stock or to SPY

universe: on the signal session: unadjusted close at least $10; average unadjusted dollar volume (close x volume) over the last 20 sessions at least $20 million; at least 131 earlier sessions of bars, with no session of the calendar missing in the 131 before it

rules.momentum: six-month return ending five sessions before the signal session: split-adjusted close 5 sessions ago over the close 131 sessions ago, minus 1
rules.leader: in the top fifth of that day's universe by momentum (the first ceil(n/5) after sorting by momentum, ties by symbol), momentum above QQQ's over the same window, and the signal session's close above its 50-session simple average
rules.pullback: three lower closes in a row (close below the previous close on the signal session and the two before it); the signal session's low at or below the 20-session exponential average of closes (span 20, started from the simple average of the first 20 closes); and average volume of those three sessions below the average of the 20 sessions before them
rules.entry: buy at the next session's open
rules.stop: if any later close is below the lowest low of the three pullback sessions, sell at the next open
rules.no_progress: if the third session's close after entry (the entry session counts as the first) is at or below the entry price, sell at the next open
rules.time: otherwise sell at the open after the tenth session's close (the entry session counts as the first)
rules.end_of_data: if a name has no further bar (delisting, halt), the last close it has, counted
rules.one_position: a new signal on a name is ignored while its earlier trade is open (until its exit session)
rules.costs: each side pays 5 basis points plus one cent a share on the unadjusted price; the stress check doubles both
rules.measure: net return per trade in percent: (exit price x (1 - exit cost)) over (entry price x (1 + entry cost)), minus 1

tests.beats_market: net return minus SPY's return from the same entry open to the same exit open (or close for an end-of-data exit), per trade
tests.pullback_adds: net return minus the mean net return of up to 5 controls: other leaders on the same signal session without a pullback signal, drawn at random (seed 20261113, in signal order), entered at the same open, exited at the same exit session's open with the same costs (a control without a bar that day exits at its last close before it)
tests.uncertainty: 2,000 bootstrap resamples of entry months (seed 20261113), each month's trades kept together; two-sided percentile interval at 97.5% (Bonferroni for two tests)

beats_market.worth a paper test: the interval's lower end is above 0, the mean is above 0 in each of the three periods, and the mean is still above 0 with doubled costs
beats_market.loses to the market: the interval's upper end is below 0

pullback_adds.the pullback adds: the interval's lower end is above 0
pullback_adds.the pullback hurts: the interval's upper end is below 0

decisions.what_each_allows: Worth a paper test: a daily after-close list on the desk with these exact rules and a paper book (stock fills at the next open) before any money; options expressions are a later, separate question. Otherwise this pullback rule is closed with no variants (other lookbacks, averages, pullback lengths or exits) on any history. The pullback_adds test says whether the pullback timing, rather than leadership alone, carries any result; plain momentum without the pullback is not decided here

descriptive_only: trades, signals skipped by the one-position rule, mean and median net return, win rate, mean hold in sessions, exits by type
costs zero; costs doubled; by year; without the best 1% of months
the controls' own return over SPY (leaders bought on a random day of leadership) and SPY's mean over the trades' holds
risk: mean return over the distance to the stop (entry minus the pullback low), as R, with a count of trades that opened at or below the stop (left out of R)
limits: daily bars fill at the open price; a real open order can fill worse in a fast open, which the cost line only approximates
dividends are left out for both sides; leaders pay little, so this slightly flatters SPY
listing snapshots every six months can miss a name listed and delisted between two snapshots
2016 snapshots are thinner (about 3,000 names against 4,500 or more later)

split-only adjustment does not handle spin-offs or a ticker reused by another company (e.g. AA in November 2016); such a day looks like a huge one-day move and can create a false stop or distorted momentum
results: Market data only: the aggregate results are committed beside this protocol after the single run; the downloaded data stays outside the repository.
one_run: one historical run under this id. A changed constant is a new protocol id, recorded beside this one
